title: Forward Deployed Software Engineer
description: About us We're solving AI's hardest problem: alignment. Encord is the data layer for Physical AI and enterprise, serving as core infrastructure for 300+ of the world's leading AI teams, including Woven by Toyota, Hitachi, Skydio, AbbVie and Dyna, Walden and Agility Robotics. From autonomous vehicles and robotics to sports and healthcare, we're solving AI's hardest problem: turning complex, real-world data into production-ready intelligent systems. We're a team of founders, scientists, quants, researchers, and former Olympians, who’ve helped build some of the most successful companies in Silicon Valley, and alumni of MIT, Stanford, UC Berkeley, Oxford, Cambridge, and Imperial. We’ve raised $110M from legendary technology investors, early backers of companies like Databricks, ElevenLabs and Vercel, and we’re growing at an extraordinary pace. We're looking for exceptional people who want to help build a category-defining company, operating with high urgency and taking real ownership to help shape the future of AI. The role We're looking for an exceptional Forward Deployed Software Engineer (FDSE) to join our engineering team. This is an engineering-first role: FDSEs are the technical owners who take the Encord platform into our most strategic and advanced customer environments, working directly with users and their engineering teams to understand complex problems, make system design decisions, and build production software that solves them. As an early member of the Forward Deployed team, you'll have an outsized impact on shaping a critical engineering function at Encord. You'll work hands-on across the stack, from APIs and data workflows to backend services and product surfaces, while owning technical problems end to end. You'll make architecture decisions under real production constraints, debug complex integrations and workflows, and build solutions that can scale beyond a single customer or use case. You'll operate autonomously, defining the right technical approach with limited guidance, building trusted relationships with users, and feeding what you learn directly back into the product and engineering roadmap. What you'll do Design and build production software for complex data, ML, and application environments Own system design decisions for deployments, balancing correctness, scalability, performance, and speed Work directly with customers and their engineering teams to understand ambiguous problems and define the right technical solution Build across the stack, from APIs and data workflows to backend systems and product-facing functionality Own deployments from technical scoping through implementation, rollout, and iteration Turn recurring customer problems into reusable tooling and product capabilities Debug complex production issues across reliability, performance, and data flow Communicate technical decisions and trade-offs clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders Operate with high autonomy and own problems end to end Feed deployment insights back into Product and Engineering, and help shape the FDSE function as the team grows Who we're looking for A strong software engineer. You have solid fundamentals and the technical depth to design and build complex production systems A first-principles problem solver. You dig into the underlying problem, challenge assumptions, and make sound technical and product trade-offs rather than defaulting to the obvious solution A strong communicator and stakeholder partner. You can build trust, navigate competing priorities, and explain complex decisions clearly An autonomous builder. You operate with limited guidance, create structure from ambiguity, and drive problems through to production A versatile product engineer. You’re comfortable working across the stack and moving between hands-on engineering, product thinking, and conversations with the people using what you build Experience requirements 4+ years of software engineering experience with strong CS fundamentals Experience building production software across the stack, from product-facing applications and APIs to backend services and data workflows Strong system design judgment and experience making architecture decisions for complex software Strong coding skills in a modern language; Python is a plus Evidence of owning technical problems end to end, from design through production Strong product judgment, technical communication, and stakeholder management Experience working directly with users, customers, or external engineering teams is a plus Bonus: experience in a high-growth startup, developer platform, or ML/data product environment Why Encord Competitive salary, commission, and meaningful equity in a high-growth startup Clear, accelerated growth opportunities as the company scales rapidly Strong in-person culture: 4 days/week Daily team lunches & dinners Annual learning & development budget Comprehensive health, dental, and vision coverage US employees: 18 paid vacation days plus US public holidays UK employees: 25 paid vacation days plus UK public holidays Frequent travel opportunities across the U.S., London, and Europe Bi-annual company offsites & monthly socials Operating principles High agency You see something broken, you fix it or find the person who can. We celebrate the people who solve 90% of a problem before anyone asks. Build with care & urgency We bear-hug the customer. Former founders and people from fast-moving, high-stakes environments thrive here. Self-aware & hungry We stay warm, self-aware, and genuinely hungry. We elevate our peers, and ego doesn't last long. Invent in real time We move toward the ambiguity. We’re pragmatic, resourceful, energized by the fact that there's no playbook. If you're looking to do the most meaningful work of your career alongside people who push you to be better, we'd love to meet you. Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Freelance Senior Technical Advisor
description: Role Details Level : Senior/ Lead Start Date : ASAP Duration : 6 months Day Rate : Dependent on experience Weekly hours : 3-4 days/ week Location : Remote Europe, GMT/BST or CET friendly Language : English, plus Spanish and/or Portuguese In this role, you’ll be a senior technical advisor to city governments across North, Central and South America, working in both an advisory and a hands-on capacity to help them design, build and launch small scale pilots of new services for residents. Working alongside experienced product managers, data scientists, AI engineers, and designers, you’ll help multidisciplinary city teams build in-house product development capability by prototyping and delivering digital products and services, many of which harness data and AI. You won’t own the decisions, but you’ll shape them. You’ll guide cities through the full product development lifecycle, helping them weigh the strategic and technical trade-offs at each stage: how to design system and data architecture that’s right-sized for a pilot but built to scale, how to prototype and test possible solutions to validate assumptions, and when AI approaches such as machine learning or large language models are the right tool (and when they aren’t). You’ll roll up your sleeves to prototype and demonstrate what good looks like, while making sure your clients understand the reasoning well enough to own the outcome. This role suits someone with the technical depth of a tech lead, and the judgement, communication skills and patience to lead through influence rather than authority. You’ll need to work fluently in English and in at least one of Spanish or Portuguese. Key skills and experiences Extensive hands-on technical experience, with strong knowledge of system and data architecture, data pipelines, DevOps and infrastructure, and a track record of delivering and deploying robust solutions end to end, from prototype to pilot, across cloud, on-premises and hybrid environments, including legacy systems and resource-constrained ones, so that your recommendations are realistic and buildable. Familiarity with AI and machine learning approaches, including large language models, and experience deploying them or working alongside ML engineers to integrate them into products, with enough understanding to judge when they’re the right tool and how to build them in responsibly. Experience taking products from early concept to first release, while laying foundations for scale, with a track record of rapid prototyping and assumption testing and a “show, don’t tell” approach that uses working prototypes to build shared understanding and inform decisions. Experience working in multidisciplinary teams, collaborating closely with product managers, designers and other disciplines throughout the product lifecycle. The ability to explain technical ideas and trade-offs clearly to audiences of all technical levels, from engineers to non-technical stakeholders and senior decision-makers. Experience setting technical direction for a project or small team and guiding other engineers, as a tech lead or senior engineer. Experience influencing technical decisions you don't directly control, whether in a consulting or advisory role or as an in-house engineer working across teams and with senior stakeholders. Curiosity and flexibility in problem solving, and comfort working through ambiguity and uncertainty in complex environments. Professional working proficiency in English and in Spanish and/or Portuguese. Nice to have Experience working with multicultural teams and on international projects. Experience working with government or other public-sector organisations, or on services for residents and citizens. Familiarity with responsible AI practices, such as data privacy, bias and fairness, transparency, and the governance considerations specific to public-sector use of AI. Experience supporting organisations to build their own technical capability, for example through coaching, mentoring or setting up new teams and practices. Our hiring process We’ve kept the process short and focused. Here’s what to expect: 1. Application & Video As part of your application, we’ll ask you to record a short video (1–3 minutes, instructions below) describing a technical project — work or personal — that you really enjoyed working on. Please record it in Spanish or Portuguese, whichever you speak fluently. You don’t need to show your face — a voiceover on a screen share, or any other format you’re comfortable with, is fine. We want to understand what the project was and why you enjoyed working on it. This isn’t a test of production quality; we’re interested in how you think and talk about your work. 2. Initial screening call A short conversation to cover the basics — your timezone, working languages, availability, and a chance for you to ask early questions about the role and how we work. 3. Technical interview (~60 minutes) A deeper conversation about your technical background and experience. We’ll talk through how you’ve approached real problems, the decisions you’ve made, and how you’d apply that thinking to the work at IF. 4. Ways of working interview (~45–60 minutes) A conversation about how you collaborate, communicate, and work with others — including how you operate in an advisory capacity with clients and teams. We’ll aim to keep you updated at every stage and let you know the outcome promptly after each step. How to record and submit your video The simplest way is Loom (free, no download needed): Go to loom.com and create a free account. Click New video → Record a video in your browser. Choose Screen and camera or Screen only if you’d prefer not to appear on camera, and make sure your microphone is selected. Record your video — remember, 1 to 3 minutes is all we need. The free plan has a 5-minute limit, which is plenty. When you stop recording, Loom will open the video and give you a link. Click Copy link . Check the sharing setting is Anyone with the link can view . Paste the link into the Link to your video field on the application form. Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Senior CRM Manager
description: We started building Marshmallow in 2017. Since then, we’ve grown from 3 to 700+ people, gained unicorn status, raised ~£140M over three funding rounds, turned profitable, insured millions of drivers and lent millions in car loans. But we’re only just getting started. Our goal is to become one of the largest financial services providers in the world. Over the next 10 years we’ll grow exponentially, not only by scaling our existing products, but also by building new ones. To achieve our goals we need incredibly ambitious, commercially driven people who never settle for ‘good enough’. Marshmallowers are hungry for autonomy and ownership, and would rather improve than coast. Everyone raises standards and has an impact, with a focus on collective success over self-interest. We’ve created an environment where curious, tenacious people win and grow together. If that sounds motivating, this could be the place for you. London (hybrid, 3 days in office) CRM at Marshmallow CRM sits within the User Experience team, helping Marshmallow build more effective, joined-up communication with our customers across the business. CRM is a meaningful driver of impact for the organisation, with clear opportunities to improve how we engage customers and measure the value of that work. This role will help shape how CRM is used at Marshmallow by building strong foundations, enabling others to use the platform effectively, and creating the governance needed to make customer communications work better across multiple teams. We’re looking for someone who is excited by ownership, enjoys working cross-functionally, and wants to help scale CRM in a thoughtful, high-impact way. This is an individual contributor role with deep platform and governance ownership, rather than a people-management track. Your impact and progression come from the scale and quality of the systems, frameworks, and cross-team relationships you build, not from growing a team. What you'll be doing Own and evolve Marshmallow’s CRM operations capability, helping shape how the platform is used across the organisation. Build strong governance frameworks for CRM activity, including how campaigns are prioritised, sequenced, and managed across teams Enable and support stakeholders across the business to use CRM effectively, increasing adoption while maintaining quality and consistency. Partner cross-functionally with teams across the organisation to identify opportunities, align on priorities, and improve customer communications. Use data and testing insights to inform decisions, optimise performance, and ensure CRM activity is driving measurable impact Drive high-quality campaign execution through strong operational processes, audience segmentation, scheduling, and platform management. Who you are You’re a self-starter who is comfortable with a high level of autonomy and enjoys taking ownership of ambiguous, high-impact work. You’re curious and collaborative , and you like working with lots of different stakeholders to move work forward. You’re someone who believes in enabling others , not gatekeeping expertise, and you’re motivated by helping teams do better work together You’re commercially minded and pragmatic , with a strong instinct for where to focus your time to unlock the most value What you'll bring Experience working in CRM operations or CRM management within an in-house, tech-led business , with a strong understanding of growth-focused customer communications. Recent hands-on experience with Braze is preferable for the role, alongside practical experience building and managing CRM campaigns, segmentation, metadata, scheduling, and audience setup Proven experience creating CRM governance and enabling other teams to use CRM effectively across an organisation Strong data literacy , including analysing campaign or email test performance, pulling audiences and segments, and working independently with data rather than relying entirely on analyst support. Confidence in using data tools or AI-assisted analysis to generate insights and support decision-making. Perks of the job Bonus scheme designed to reward high performance Private medical insurance with Vitality, mental health support with Oliva Personal learning budget and 2 dedicated L&D days a year Monthly flexible benefits budget to spend as you choose 25 days holiday plus bank holidays 4 weeks Work From Anywhere per year We are able to offer visa sponsorship for this position. Our process Initial call with a member from our Talent Team (30 mins) Past Experience interview with Hiring Manager (60 mins) Onsite case study interview with a couple of the team (90 mins) Culture interview (60 mins) Diversity of thought We know the best ideas come from having different perspectives in the room - and we're committed to hiring fairly, regardless of background, identity or experience. If you see yourself in this role, we'd encourage you to apply. Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Director, International Expansion — CEO Office
description: About Airwallex Airwallex is the AI-native financial operating system for a real-time, intelligent economy. More than 675,000 businesses, including McLaren Racing, Qantas, SHEIN, and TikTok, use us, directly or through our platform partners, to run their financial operations or build and monetize financial products of their own. We started in Melbourne in 2015 to build the infrastructure global commerce runs on. We're the regulated backbone behind global payments: not by accident, but by design. A decade plus, 85+ licenses, and a financial infrastructure spanning North America, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific. We're co-headquartered in San Francisco and Singapore, with more than 2,700 people across 27 offices. We hire builders with founder-level energy, people who move fast with good judgment, dig in with real curiosity, and make calls from first principles rather than waiting to be told what to do. description: Join Pigment: The AI Platform Redefining Business Planning Pigment is the AI-powered business planning and performance management platform built for agility and scale. Founded in 2019, Pigment is one of the fastest-growing SaaS companies globally. Industry leaders like Unilever, Uber, Anthropic, Snowflake or Siemens, use Pigment daily to make more informed decisions and confidently navigate any scenario. With a team of 700+ across Paris, London, New York, Toronto, San Francisco and Austin, we've raised nearly $400M from top-tier investors and were named a Visionary in the 2024 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Financial Planning Software. At Pigment, we take smart risks, celebrate bold ideas, and challenge the status quo - all while working as one team. If you're driven by innovation and ready to make an impact at scale, we’d love to hear from you. We're hiring an Engineering Manager who wants to spend 80% of their time writing code, not attending management meetings. About the role Are you an experienced Software Engineer who loves writing code, solving complex technical problems and helping other engineers become better at what they do? At Pigment, our Engineering Managers are engineers first. Unlike traditional Engineering Manager positions, this role is designed for someone who wants to remain deeply involved in building software while taking on meaningful people-management responsibilities. You'll spend approximately 80% of your time designing, coding and shipping production features , with the remaining 20% dedicated to coaching engineers, running regular 1:1s, providing feedback and supporting their development. We're particularly interested in Senior Software Engineers who have naturally taken on coaching, mentoring or technical leadership responsibilities and are ready to develop further as people managers. You don't necessarily need to have held an Engineering Manager title before. What matters most is your technical ability, your experience helping others grow and your motivation to combine engineering with people leadership. You'll join Pigment's Reporting & Collaboration community, building sophisticated frontend experiences that help customers interact with complex data, configure workflows and make better business decisions. What you'll do 🧑‍💻 Software Engineering (80%) You'll remain an active contributor to our production codebase, working alongside other engineers on challenging frontend projects. Write, review, refactor and ship production code regularly using React, TypeScript and JavaScript. Design and build sophisticated user interfaces for interacting with large datasets, including filtering, visualisation and complex configuration. Take ownership of engineering tasks and features from technical design through implementation, testing and deployment. Solve challenging problems involving frontend performance, scalability, state management and user experience. Participate in technical discussions, code reviews, debugging and architectural decisions. Collaborate closely with Product Managers, Designers, Tech Leads and Software Engineers to deliver high-quality features. Contribute to AI-powered product experiences and use modern development tools where appropriate. Maintain the same technical expectations and engineering standards as our Senior Software Engineers. You'll continue to write production code, not simply oversee the engineers who do. 📚 Coaching & People Management (20%) Alongside your engineering responsibilities, you'll help other engineers develop their skills, confidence and careers. Coach and mentor engineers, sharing technical knowledge and helping them improve their problem-solving abilities. Hold regular 1:1 meetings with your direct reports to discuss progress, challenges and career development. Provide constructive feedback, recognise achievements and support individual development plans. Help engineers establish clear goals and understand the skills required to progress. Support performance reviews and development discussions, including more challenging conversations when necessary. Work alongside Tech Leads to understand engineers' technical contributions and development needs. Help foster a collaborative engineering culture where people continuously learn from one another. At Pigment, technical leadership and people management are intentionally separated. Tech Leads own the technical direction of teams, while Engineering Managers focus on coaching and developing engineers alongside their own coding responsibilities. You'll initially focus on contributing as a Senior Engineer before gradually taking on direct reports. Who we're looking for You're an engineer first, with a genuine interest in developing people. You have substantial professional software-engineering experience and are technically operating at a strong Senior Engineer level. You're currently hands-on with production code and want coding to remain the majority of your working week. You have strong frontend development experience with React, TypeScript and JavaScript. You've built complex, scalable applications, ideally within B2B SaaS, enterprise software, analytics or data-intensive environments. You have experience coaching, mentoring or supporting other engineers through code reviews, pairing, technical discussions or structured feedback. You enjoy sharing knowledge and helping other engineers improve. You're interested in taking ownership of 1:1s, career development and people-management responsibilities, or already have experience doing so. You're comfortable solving complex technical challenges independently while collaborating with others. You care about product quality, engineering standards and delivering meaningful value to customers. You're fluent in English. French is not required. Previous formal people-management experience is a plus, but not a requirement. We're equally interested in strong Senior Engineers who have demonstrated the ability to coach others and are ready to take the next step. You want to develop people-management skills without moving away from engineering. You enjoy the challenge of balancing meaningful individual contributions with coaching responsibilities. title: Senior Product Manager, Search Infrastructure
description: <h3><strong><span data-ccp-props="{}">The role</span></strong></h3> <p>Tavily, part of Nebius, is the web access layer for AI agents. Over two million developers use us, and our customers include Fortune 500 companies running agents in production.</p> <p>We build and run our own index. That means we own the hard problems directly: crawl coverage at scale, freshness, cost per query, and the quality of what comes back. This role owns that infrastructure as a product.</p> <p>When an agent asks a question, the answer has to be relevant, fresh, fast, and affordable. Those four things pull against each other, and someone has to decide which one gives. That is you. You will set what good means for each use case we serve and the bar a change has to clear before it ships, working closely with our evaluation team, who own how we measure it. You will also shape where our index goes next: what it needs to cover, how fresh it needs to be, and what it has to be good at.</p> <p>The most open part of the job is what comes next. Search is being rebuilt for a consumer that is not a person. Agents do not want one result page, they want to break a problem apart, run many retrievals, and decide what to do next. That changes what search infrastructure should look like, and part of your job is to have a view on where ours should go.</p> <p>The hard part is deciding what good enough means. Perfect coverage, perfect freshness, and low cost cannot all be true at once, and the person in this seat is the one who has to make that call for each use case and defend it.</p> <p>In your first year, we expect you to set a clear quality bar for our search products that the team builds against, have a real influence on where our index goes next, and bring us a point of view on where search infrastructure is heading.</p> <p>This is a hands-on senior IC role with real ownership, reporting to the Director of Product. You will work day to day with our search engineering and research teams, with the evaluation team, and with customer success, who bring us quality feedback from real accounts every week. Our search engineers are deeply experienced in large-scale retrieval, and the product team is small, so you will argue your case directly with the people building it. title: Senior Campaign Manager (Temp Contract)
description: About Pleo Messy spend management is tricky business. And tedious processes are a lose-lose situation for all involved, not just finance. At Pleo, we're changing that. We build spend solutions that make managing money seamless, empowering, and surprisingly effective for finance teams and employees alike - with a vision to help all businesses ‘go beyond’. The word ‘Pleo’ actually means ‘more than you’d expect’, and living by that mantra has been the secret to our success over the last 10 years. Now, we’re at a pivotal moment in our journey; every move we make has a direct impact on our 40,000+ customers, our business, and our collective success. We need people who take pride in uncovering customer needs, who turn complex problems into simple solutions, challenge the way things are done (respectfully), and always aim high. With great ambitions driving us forward, we can’t say we’ve got this whole thing figured out. And frankly, that’s half the fun! What we can say is that we’re a driven, progressive, and, importantly, a kind bunch of 850+ people from over 100 nationalities, all committed to delivering the future of business spending, together. About the role We're looking for a Senior Integrated Campaign Manager, Brand & GTM to join our Integrated Marketing team at Pleo. In this role, you'll help architect, roll out, project manage, and drive the Go-To-Market (GTM) execution for our major 2027 brand marketing strategy and campaigns and be part of turning brand strategy, positioning, and creative concepts into operational GTM blueprints as we scale our multi-segment (SMB, Mid-Market, Enterprise) reach across 6 key European markets. If you're excited about high-visibility, full-funnel orchestration and balancing long-term brand equity building with full-funnel conversion, and are passionate about integrated brand and GTM marketing in high-growth B2B SaaS, then this is the opportunity for you! Please bear in mind this role is a temporary contract of 1 year. Who you’ll be working with and reporting to You’ll report to our Director of Integrated Marketing and work closely with teams in Brand Marketing, Digital, Field/Events, Content, PR, Product Marketing (PMM), Marketing Ops, Data, and Sales/Growth channels. Our team is highly collaborative and dedicated to bridging top-of-funnel brand awareness with lower-funnel acquisition, ensuring every campaign moment translates into market salience, customer engagement, and measurable business impact. You’ll also have the chance to partner with teams across country teams, local market stakeholders, Sales Leadership, SDRs, and Field squads to ensure success. What you’ll be doing As a Senior Campaign Manager, you will: Integrated GTM Architecture & Strategic Planning : Translate the overarching 2027 brand strategy into actionable, full-funnel GTM campaign blueprints across SMB, Mid-Market, and Enterprise segments, architecting campaign flighting and distribution models across 6 European markets. The "Master Brief" & Cross-Functional Squad Leadership : Own and author comprehensive Integrated Campaign Master Briefs, leading the operational rhythm of cross-functional squads to execute multi-channel strategies (OOH, Paid Social, VIP activations, Digital, ABM) on time and within scope. Localization & Regional Adaptation : Partner with country teams and local market stakeholders to ensure master campaign frameworks balance global consistency with local relevance and execution precision. Strategic Brand Partnership & Enablement : Serve as the strategic execution peer to the Brand Marketing Lead, while partnering with Sales Leadership, SDRs, and Field teams to equip customer-facing squads with the stories, tools, and campaign momentum needed to capitalize on campaign-generated intent. Campaign Operations, Budget & ROI Accountability : Maintain and protect the integrated campaign master calendar, manage and allocate the multi-country integrated campaign budget, and partner with Marketing Ops, Data, and Brand Intelligence to track brand lift, consideration, pipeline growth, and closed-won impact. What you bring You’ll thrive in this role if you have: A proven track record leading multi-million dollar, multi-country, full-funnel integrated campaigns in high-growth B2B SaaS or tech environments. Deep experience taking high-level brand frameworks and translating them into multi-channel GTM blueprints across varied audience segments (SMB to Enterprise). High proficiency in aligning cross-functional teams (Creative, Digital, PR, Ops, Sales) and holding squads accountable to tight deadlines and complex campaign launches. Deep understanding of how to run campaigns across diverse European markets, with a clear perspective on modular campaign design and local adaptation. Experience with tracking brand-to-pipeline performance metrics, campaign flighting dynamics, brand lift, consideration, and total ROI. A background in integrated marketing, GTM campaign management, or brand marketing orchestration within B2B technology or SaaS. Why is this role a good fit for you This role is a good fit for you if: You thrive as the operational bridge between high-level brand strategy and lower-funnel demand generation, turning concepts into structured GTM blueprints. You love leading cross-functional squads across multiple international markets, balancing consistency with local nuances across 6 key European countries. You take pride in end-to-end accountability, from authoring master briefs and handling multi-country budgets to tracking downstream pipeline velocity and closed-won revenue impact. This role is not a good fit for you if: You prefer focusing purely on high-level creative ideation, copy, or audience insight development without building the operational execution machinery. You prefer running single-channel or single-market marketing initiatives rather than orchestrating complex, multi-segment (SMB to Enterprise), multi-channel matrices. You are uncomfortable navigating data, campaign flighting performance, budget allocations, and downstream pipeline attribution alongside brand metrics. How you’ll develop in this role In your first 6 months at Pleo, you’ll: Lead the architecture and rollout of the 2027 integrated brand campaign calendar across all target European markets. Collaborate with the Brand Marketing Lead, country teams, and Marketing Ops to stand up the Master Briefing framework and streamline cross-functional execution rhythms. Grow your skills in full-funnel orchestration and multi-market scale, driving measurable brand lift, consideration, and downstream pipeline velocity as Pleo continues to expand. The location Please note: We can hire on a hybrid or in-person set-up in any of the locations listed on the advert but you will need to be physically based in the country of your choice with a valid right to work . We are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role in any of the listed locations. Show me the benefits! Your own Pleo card (no more out-of-pocket spending!) Lunch is on us for your work days - enjoy catered meals or receive a lunch allowance based on your local office Comprehensive private healthcare - depending on your location, coverage options include Vitality, Alan or Médis 25 days of annual leave + public holidays (additional days may apply in select countries based on local standards). For our Team, we offer both hybrid and fully remote working options We use MyndUp to give our employees access to free mental health and well-being support with great success so far Paid parental leave - we want to make sure that we're supportive of families and help you feel that you don't have to compromise your family due to work The interview process We want to ensure you are set-up for success and understand what will be expected of you. If your application is successful, our interview process is as follows: Intro call: A 30-minute chat with our Talent Partner to discuss the role and your background. Hiring Manager Interview: A 45 minute chat to deep dive into your experience Challenge & Team Interview: We will send you a take home test and invite you to present during a 60 minute team interview. This is an opportunity to show us how you would handle the day to day of the role Final Interview : A final interview with a senior leader Transparency is important to us so we also wanted to share some insights about what we’re looking for in applications to ensure you can set yourself up for success! Last time we hired for this role, we received a total vast number of applications but only a few were selected for an intro call.Some of the key reasons why previous candidates didn’t make it past the application screening stage include: CV writing and content: we receive a lot of CVs, and many of them are AI-generated. We love seeing people leverage AI—it’s a big focus for us internally too—but without human intervention, these CVs can sometimes become generic and fail to show a candidate in the best light. What we're really looking for is the specific details of real impact that only you know from your previous experience. A top tip from us is to use the “Achieved X, as measured by Y, by doing Z” formula (credit: Laszlo Bock, ~2014) to give a really clear picture of what you’ve worked on. A final note: including links to your previous companies' websites is a huge help and allows us to truly understand your background! Application care: every single application we receive is reviewed by a human (yes, hundreds of them) because we believe that candidates' efforts should be matched by an equal level of human care. This means that we expect a similar level of attention put into your application. Read and answer the application questions carefully, they make a huge difference in our decision-making process. Profile to role fit: highlight most important aspects of the role, points that might get misunderstood, any specific industry requirements etc. About your application English first. Since it's our company language, please submit your application in English. You’ll be using it a lot if you join us. A fair look for everyone. Our talent team reads every single application to ensure the process is fair. To keep things running smoothly, we only accept applications through our system—our support team can’t pass on calls or emails. Diversity drives us. We can only reach our goals if our team reflects the world around us. That starts with you hitting apply, even if you don't tick every single box. We encourage people from all backgrounds and experiences to join us. Interview at your best. We want you to feel comfortable throughout the process. If you have any accessibility requirements or need a specific format, email ----- We’ll design a process that works for you. Your data is safe. When you apply, we process your personal data as a data processor. For more information on how Pleo processes personal data, read our Privacy Policy here . Applying for multiple roles? Nothing is stopping you, and we assess every role independently. However, we do look for alignment, so make sure you can explain why your interest and experience are right for each specific role. Reapplying. If you’re applying for the same role again, please wait six months from your last decision before hitting submit. Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

description: About Pleo Messy spend management is tricky business. And tedious processes are a lose-lose situation for all involved, not just finance. At Pleo, we're changing that. We need people who take pride in uncovering customer needs, who turn complex problems into simple solutions, challenge the way things are done (respectfully), and always aim high. With great ambitions driving us forward, we can’t say we’ve got this whole thing figured out. And frankly, that’s half the fun! What we can say is that we’re a driven, progressive, and, importantly, a kind bunch of 850+ people from over 100 nationalities, all committed to delivering the future of business spending, together. About the role We're looking for a Staff Security Operations Engineer to join our Cybersecurity team at Pleo. In this role, you'll define and deliver the SecOps roadmap, building the detection, response, and investigation capability that protects a fast-growing fintech. If you're excited about owning a security operations function end to end, from framework-based strategy through to the code that makes it run, then this is the opportunity for you! Who you'll be working with and reporting to You'll report to our VP of Fraud & Security and work closely with Fraud, DevSecOps, Engineering, and Risk & Compliance. Our team is highly collaborative and dedicated to protecting Pleo's customers and their money. You'll also have the chance to partner with teams across the organisation and to bring less experienced security engineers up with you as the function matures. What you'll be doing As a Staff Security Operations Engineer, you will: Build and own a structured SecOps roadmap grounded in well-known frameworks such as MITRE ATT&CK, NIST, and CIS benchmarks. Lead security investigations and digital forensics, from suspicious traffic through to full incident response, and bring the findings back into how we detect and prevent. Design, tune, and scale our SIEM and logging pipeline through standardized log ingestion across services so signal isn't lost in the noise. Strengthen our perimeter and authentication posture, including WAF configuration, authorisation tuning, and monitoring for suspicious traffic. Protect sensitive data through DLP controls, and make sure the coverage matches where the data actually lives. Improve our on-call rotation for the team, defining the alerting, escalation paths, and response SLAs that make it work. Automate detection and response workflows, using code and AI to reduce manual toil and shorten time to resolution. Reduce SecOps-attributed risk identified through compliance gaps, and collect the evidence that demonstrates it. Build dashboards and reporting that give the team and leadership real visibility into response times, coverage, and risk reduction. Work cross-functionally with engineers who don't have a security background, translating threat models into changes they can actually ship. What you bring You'll thrive in this role if you have: 10+ years of experience in security operations, incident response, or a closely related discipline, with a proven track record of materialised risk reduction through monetary impact, incidents contained, forensics that changed outcomes. A strong development and engineering background. You are comfortable writing the automation, not just specifying it. Hands-on SOC and SIEM management experience, including detection engineering and log pipeline design. Experience in scale-up environments, where you've built capability rather than inherited a mature one. A strong understanding of cloud architectures as we use AWS. With part of our estate on GCP and how infrastructure decisions shape detection and response. Demonstrated experience using AI and/or coding automation to get security controls built, implemented, and operating in practice. Fintech, payments, fraud, or trust & safety experience is a real advantage, as is exposure to highly regulated environments. Backgrounds that tend to do well here: incident response, IR management, SOC engineering, security engineering, DevSecOps, red or blue team. Why is this role a good fit for you This role is a good fit for you if: You want a large blast radius. We have high-impact projects where the outcome shows up in real business metrics, at a pre-IPO company. You're energised by building a function rather than maintaining one, and you'd rather set the roadmap than be handed it. You enjoy raising the bar around you, growing a team of specialists and lifting the people already here. You're equally at home in a threat model discussion and in an editor writing the automation that acts on it. This role is not a good fit for you if: You need a well-groomed backlog and assigned tasks in order to do your best work. You'd rather stay purely strategic than get hands-on with the tooling. You're not up for participating in an on-call rotation. How you'll develop in this role In your first 6 months at Pleo, you'll: Get deep into Pleo's security landscape and our detection coverage, our logging estate, our cloud footprint to form your own view of where the biggest risks sit. Publish a SecOps roadmap mapped to MITRE, NIST, and CIS, agree with Engineering, Risk & Compliance, and leadership, and start delivering against it. Stand up the on-call rotation and the alert response SLAs that go with it. Ship your first wave of detection and automation improvements, and establish the KPIs that show what changed. We're committed to helping you develop your career, whether that means taking on bigger projects, stepping into leadership, or acquiring new skills. There's genuine room here for the scope of this role to grow, including into people leadership. The location Please note: We can hire on a remote, hybrid or in-person set-up in any of the locations listed on the advert but you will need to be physically based in the country of your choice with a valid right to work. We are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role in any of the listed locations. Show me the benefits! Your own Pleo card (no more out-of-pocket spending!) Lunch is on us for your work days - enjoy catered meals or receive a lunch allowance based on your local office Comprehensive private healthcare - depending on your location, coverage options include Vitality, Alan or Médis We offer 25-28 days of holiday (depending on your location) + public holidays For our Team, we offer both hybrid and fully remote working options Option to purchase 5 additional days of holiday through a salary sacrifice We use MyndUp to give our employees access to free mental health and well-being support with great success so far Paid parental leave - we want to make sure that we're supportive of families and help you feel that you don't have to compromise your family due to work The interview process We want to ensure you are set-up for success and understand what will be expected of you. If your application is successful, our interview process is as follows: Intro call: A 30-minute chat with our Talent Partner to discuss the role and your background. Hiring Manager interview: a 60-minute conversation covering your experience, how you approach security operations, and how you communicate. Technical deep dive: a 60-minute session with two of our SecOps engineers, going deep on SIEM, detection engineering, your coding and automation experience. Cross-functional interview: a 45-minute conversation with DevSecOps and Engineering leadership on how you work across team boundaries with other senior engineers. About your application English first. Since it's our company language, please submit your application in English. You’ll be using it a lot if you join us. A fair look for everyone. title: Staff Security Operations Engineer
description: About Pleo Messy spend management is tricky business. And tedious processes are a lose-lose situation for all involved, not just finance. At Pleo, we're changing that. We build spend solutions that make managing money seamless, empowering, and surprisingly effective for finance teams and employees alike - with a vision to help all businesses ‘go beyond’. The word ‘Pleo’ actually means ‘more than you’d expect’, and living by that mantra has been the secret to our success over the last 10 years. Now, we’re at a pivotal moment in our journey; every move we make has a direct impact on our 40,000+ customers, our business, and our collective success. We need people who take pride in uncovering customer needs, who turn complex problems into simple solutions, challenge the way things are done (respectfully), and always aim high. With great ambitions driving us forward, we can’t say we’ve got this whole thing figured out. And frankly, that’s half the fun! What we can say is that we’re a driven, progressive, and, importantly, a kind bunch of 850+ people from over 100 nationalities, all committed to delivering the future of business spending, together. About the role We're looking for a Staff Security Operations Engineer to join our Cybersecurity team at Pleo. In this role, you'll define and deliver the SecOps roadmap, building the detection, response, and investigation capability that protects a fast-growing fintech. If you're excited about owning a security operations function end to end, from framework-based strategy through to the code that makes it run, then this is the opportunity for you! Who you'll be working with and reporting to You'll report to our VP of Fraud & Security and work closely with Fraud, DevSecOps, Engineering, and Risk & Compliance. Our team is highly collaborative and dedicated to protecting Pleo's customers and their money. You'll also have the chance to partner with teams across the organisation and to bring less experienced security engineers up with you as the function matures. What you'll be doing As a Staff Security Operations Engineer, you will: Build and own a structured SecOps roadmap grounded in well-known frameworks such as MITRE ATT&CK, NIST, and CIS benchmarks. Lead security investigations and digital forensics, from suspicious traffic through to full incident response, and bring the findings back into how we detect and prevent. Design, tune, and scale our SIEM and logging pipeline through standardized log ingestion across services so signal isn't lost in the noise. Strengthen our perimeter and authentication posture, including WAF configuration, authorisation tuning, and monitoring for suspicious traffic. Protect sensitive data through DLP controls, and make sure the coverage matches where the data actually lives. Improve our on-call rotation for the team, defining the alerting, escalation paths, and response SLAs that make it work. Automate detection and response workflows, using code and AI to reduce manual toil and shorten time to resolution. Reduce SecOps-attributed risk identified through compliance gaps, and collect the evidence that demonstrates it. Build dashboards and reporting that give the team and leadership real visibility into response times, coverage, and risk reduction. Work cross-functionally with engineers who don't have a security background, translating threat models into changes they can actually ship. What you bring You'll thrive in this role if you have: 10+ years of experience in security operations, incident response, or a closely related discipline, with a proven track record of materialised risk reduction through monetary impact, incidents contained, forensics that changed outcomes. A strong development and engineering background. You are comfortable writing the automation, not just specifying it. Hands-on SOC and SIEM management experience, including detection engineering and log pipeline design. Experience in scale-up environments, where you've built capability rather than inherited a mature one. A strong understanding of cloud architectures as we use AWS. With part of our estate on GCP and how infrastructure decisions shape detection and response. Demonstrated experience using AI and/or coding automation to get security controls built, implemented, and operating in practice. Fintech, payments, fraud, or trust & safety experience is a real advantage, as is exposure to highly regulated environments. Backgrounds that tend to do well here: incident response, IR management, SOC engineering, security engineering, DevSecOps, red or blue team. Why is this role a good fit for you This role is a good fit for you if: You want a large blast radius. We have high-impact projects where the outcome shows up in real business metrics, at a pre-IPO company. You're energised by building a function rather than maintaining one, and you'd rather set the roadmap than be handed it. You enjoy raising the bar around you, growing a team of specialists and lifting the people already here. You're equally at home in a threat model discussion and in an editor writing the automation that acts on it. This role is not a good fit for you if: You need a well-groomed backlog and assigned tasks in order to do your best work. You'd rather stay purely strategic than get hands-on with the tooling. You're not up for participating in an on-call rotation. How you'll develop in this role In your first 6 months at Pleo, you'll: Get deep into Pleo's security landscape and our detection coverage, our logging estate, our cloud footprint to form your own view of where the biggest risks sit. Publish a SecOps roadmap mapped to MITRE, NIST, and CIS, agree with Engineering, Risk & Compliance, and leadership, and start delivering against it. Stand up the on-call rotation and the alert response SLAs that go with it. Ship your first wave of detection and automation improvements, and establish the KPIs that show what changed. We're committed to helping you develop your career, whether that means taking on bigger projects, stepping into leadership, or acquiring new skills. There's genuine room here for the scope of this role to grow, including into people leadership. The location Please note: We can hire on a remote, hybrid or in-person set-up in any of the locations listed on the advert but you will need to be physically based in the country of your choice with a valid right to work. Lunch is on us for your work days - enjoy catered meals or receive a lunch allowance based on your local office Comprehensive private healthcare - depending on your location, coverage options include Vitality, Alan or Médis We offer 25-28 days of holiday (depending on your location) + public holidays For our Team, we offer both hybrid and fully remote working options Option to purchase 5 additional days of holiday through a salary sacrifice We use MyndUp to give our employees access to free mental health and well-being support with great success so far Paid parental leave - we want to make sure that we're supportive of families and help you feel that you don't have to compromise your family due to work The interview process We want to ensure you are set-up for success and understand what will be expected of you. If your application is successful, our interview process is as follows: Intro call: A 30-minute chat with our Talent Partner to discuss the role and your background. Technical deep dive: a 60-minute session with two of our SecOps engineers, going deep on SIEM, detection engineering, your coding and automation experience. Cross-functional interview: a 45-minute conversation with DevSecOps and Engineering leadership on how you work across team boundaries with other senior engineers. title: Principal Software Engineer
description: You’ll be a Technical Leader, unblock the engineering team by resolving complex technical impasses, standardising engineering practices, and owning cross-functional initiatives. You'll still be a highly hands-on engineer, responsible for rapidly prototyping, shipping MVPs, and turning product ideas into polished user experiences. You’ll work across the stack, collaborating closely with product, design, and engineering teams while operating with a high degree of independence. What you'll do Build and ship new product features end-to-end Lead rapid prototyping and MVP development Develop modern frontend applications using TypeScript, Vue 3 Composition API, and Tailwind Contribute to backend services using Node, Bun, Koa, PostgreSQL, Prisma, and AWS Collaborate closely with cross-functional teams to shape product direction Improve performance, reliability, and developer experience across the platfor Support on hiring, performance and technical roadmaps. What you'll need Extensive experience building modern frontend applications with TypeScript and Vue3 Solid backend experience with Node-based services and relational databases Experience working with PostgreSQL, Prisma, AWS, and REST APIs Comfortable moving quickly, making pragmatic decisions, and shipping iteratively Strong communication and collaboration skills Able to work independently in a hybrid environment Ideally have been in early stage start-ups going through growth and technical challenges What you'll get Time off that works for you: Unlimited holiday policy, including a guaranteed 33 days plus your birthday off Flexible hybrid working: Work in a way that helps you do your best work, while staying connected with the team. A stake in what we’re building: Eligible employees can participate in our EMI share option scheme. Healthcare that goes further: After one year’s service, access private healthcare through Vitality, including dental, optical, hearing and therapy cover. More ways to get around: Access our company car salary-sacrifice scheme. Support for growing families: Enhanced maternity and paternity leave. About Cytix Software never stops changing. Teams ship new code every day, through tickets, pull requests, releases, and increasingly with AI in the mix, but the way security keeps up with all that change hasn't really moved on. That's the problem we're solving. Cytix helps organisations understand which software changes actually matter, what should happen next, and how to prove the right call was made. Security understood, in other words. We're a small team with big plans, so every person we hire genuinely shapes what Cytix becomes. That's why we're upfront about our five values: we interview for all of them, and they matter to us more than a perfect CV. They're things you do, not things you are, so have a read and see if they sound like you. Make the first move. When the goal is clear but the path isn't, you get moving rather than waiting for perfect instructions. If you're blocked, you make a sensible call, say what you're assuming, and explain how you'd course-correct. We'd rather you act and be slightly wrong than sit still. Find the smarter path. You ask why before how. You dig into what the real problem is instead of just building what the spec says, and you're happy to question 'that's how it's always been done' when the reason behind it has gone stale. See it through. When something's yours, it lands. No loose ends, no surprises for whoever picks it up next. You keep people posted when things change, and if something falls between roles, you catch it. Raise the bar. You do the best job possible in the time you've got, whether that's a day or a month. Sometimes that means deep craft; sometimes the smartest move is quick and scrappy. It's about good judgement, and we hold each other to it without blame or politics. Play to win. You care about the mission but don't take yourself too seriously. You say 'I' when things go wrong and 'we' when they go right, trust teammates to do things their own way, and bring a bit of humour when the pressure's on. Sound like you on a normal working day? We'd love to meet you. Compensation: £100K – £120K • Equity • £100K – £120K • Equity Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Senior Partner Manager (German speaking)
description: About Us Perk (formerly TravelPerk) is the intelligent platform for travel and spend management. Built to tackle the time-consuming, manual work that gets in the way of real work, our tools automate everything from travel bookings to expenses, invoice processing, and more. By eliminating this shadow work that wastes hours, erodes morale, and saps innovation, we're on a mission to power real work, with real impact. We're trusted by more than 12,000 companies worldwide, including Bolt, GoCardless, and Fabletics, and we're tackling the 7 hours of lost productivity per employee each week, a $1.7 trillion problem . Founded in 2015, Perk has grown into a global company of more than 1,800 people across 12 offices globally, with headquarters in London and Boston. We combine innovation, control, and simplicity to transform how businesses work and how people feel at work. At Perk, we're driven by our values, like being an owner, delivering a 7-star experience, and working as one team. We value curiosity, purpose, and mindset, not just knowledge, to unlock the power in your potential. Our talent team brings together leading minds from the travel, fintech, and SaaS industries, representing over 70 countries. If you're excited about having a real impact and shaping how millions of people experience work, we'd love you on the team. Visit www.perk.com to learn more. About the Role We’re looking for an ambitious, German-speaking Senior Partner Manager (Strategic Partnerships) to build and scale Perk’s partner ecosystem across Europe, with a particular focus on the DACH region. This is a commercial role with a clear objective: build partnerships that generate qualified sales pipeline and revenue for Perk. You’ll identify and recruit the right partners, develop joint go-to-market strategies, and turn those relationships into a repeatable growth channel. You’ll work closely with Sales and Marketing while owning partner relationships from initial outreach through launch, activation, and ongoing performance. The ideal person combines a builder’s mindset with strong commercial instincts. You’re comfortable opening doors, creating something from scratch, and earning the trust of senior stakeholders. You’re ambitious, persistent, and focused on measurable results. What You’ll Do Build our partner ecosystem: Identify, recruit, and develop high-potential referral, reseller, technology, and strategic alliance partners across Europe, with a particular focus on DACH. Generate pipeline and revenue: Own partner-sourced and partner-influenced pipeline targets, turning partnerships into a meaningful and repeatable growth channel for Perk. Create joint go-to-market strategies: Build plans with priority partners across target accounts, campaigns, events, referrals, and co-selling motions. Own the commercial relationship: Lead partner conversations from initial outreach through business case development, negotiation, contracting, launch, and ongoing growth. Activate and enable partners: Give partners the product knowledge, sales materials, training, and support they need to confidently position Perk and identify opportunities. Partner closely with Sales and Marketing: Ensure partner-generated opportunities are effectively routed, prioritised, and converted, while creating scalable ways for our commercial teams to work with partners. Measure and improve performance: Set targets, forecast partner pipeline and revenue, identify what’s working, and continuously improve our partnership strategy and playbooks. Bring new opportunities to Perk: Stay close to market and product developments and identify new partner models that can accelerate growth or create meaningful value for our customers. What We’re Looking For Languages: Native or near-native fluency in German and professional fluency in English. Track record: Proven success in partnerships, alliances, channel sales, or business development, ideally within SaaS, fintech, travel technology, or another B2B technology environment. ERP and finance technology ecosystem : Hands on experience working with ERP, accounting and finance automation vendors and their partner ecosystems (e.g Netsuite, Microsoft Dynamics, Sage, Xero, Datev). Commercial performance: A history of building partnerships that generate measurable sales pipeline and revenue against targets. Builder mentality: Comfortable developing new partner relationships and go-to-market motions from scratch rather than simply managing an established programme. Executive presence: Strong communication and presentation skills, with the credibility to build relationships and negotiate with senior and C-level stakeholders. Commercial judgment: Able to assess which opportunities are worth pursuing, structure mutually valuable partnerships, and focus time on the relationships most likely to produce meaningful results. Cross-functional mindset: A low-ego, team-first approach and the ability to work effectively across Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, Product, and other teams. Ownership: Independent, ambitious, persistent, and comfortable being accountable for outcomes. Based within commuting distance of our hub. Travel: Willingness to travel regularly across Europe for partner meetings, conferences and events. What we offer Receive competitive compensation and equity ownership in Perk Rest and recharge with 25 days of annual leave plus bank holidays Take control of your physical health with private medical cover and voluntary dental insurance from Bupa, and discounted gym memberships with GymFlex Plan for your future with our qualifying earnings company pension plan with Aviva Know that your loved ones are protected financially through your Life Insurance if the worst were to happen Rest assured that you’re covered by income protection in case you experience a long-term sickness or absence Leverage tax-efficient cycle and electric car schemes with Cycle2Work & Octopus Join our unforgettable Perk events, including our spectacular annual summer party Always feel supported with Spring Health, our market-leading wellbeing partner, providing fast, comprehensive access to 12x therapy and 12x coaching sessions for you and your loved ones Focus on your family with 12-16 weeks’ paid parental leave Contribute to your community with 16 paid hours per year to spend volunteering for your dearest charitable causes Broaden your horizons with up to 20 "Work from Anywhere" days per year Stay savvy with access to a wide variety of discounts and rewards Follow your passions and take a four-week, fully paid sabbatical once you reach 5 years Let us help you move to one of our hubs with relocation support Interview Process Talent Acquisition Interview - 30mins Virtual Hiring Manager Interview - 30mins Virtual Assessment Interview - 60mins - Virtual Values interview - 30mins virtual AI at Perk AI is embedded in how we work across every function. The tools you'll use day-to-day are AI-enabled so you can move faster and spend more time on the work that matters. In practice, that means using AI to research and prioritise accounts, draft and refine outreach, handle customer interactions more effectively, synthesise information, and cut through shadow work - the invisible tasks that pull people away from the work only they can do - so you can focus on relationships and outcomes. How We Work At Perk, we take an IRL-first approach to work, where our team works together in-person 3 days a week. As such, this role requires you to be based within commuting distance of our hubs. We fundamentally believe in the value of meeting in real life to improve connectivity, productivity, creativity and ultimately making us a great place to work. For certain roles, we can help with relocation from anywhere in the world, English is the official language at the office. Please submit your resume in English if you choose to apply. Do not forget to submit an updated portfolio and/or resume. Perk is a global company with a diverse customer base, and we want to make sure the people behind our product reflect that. We’re an equal opportunity employer, which means you’re welcome at Perk regardless of how you look, where you’re from, or anything else that makes you, well, you. Protect Yourself from Recruitment Scams All official communication from Perk will always come from email addresses ending in @ perk.com or @ externalperk.com , our verified social media channels, or recruiters listed on our official LinkedIn page. We will never ask you to pay for equipment, training, or fees, request sensitive personal information such as bank details early in the process, or communicate through unofficial apps like WhatsApp, Telegram, or Signal. If you receive a message claiming to be from Perk that seems suspicious, please do not respond. Forward it to security [at] perk .com , and we will confirm whether it is legitimate. #LI-Hybrid Find Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Product Designer
description: Our mission We're making Africa the first cashless continent. In 2017, over half the population in Sub-Saharan Africa had no bank account. That's for good reason—the fees are too high, the closest branch can be miles away, and nobody takes cards. Without access to financial institutions, people are forced to keep their savings under the mattress. Small business owners rely on lenders who charge extortionate rates. Parents spend hours waiting in line to pay school fees in cash. We're solving this by building financial services that just work: no account fees, instantly available, and accepted everywhere. In places where electricity, water and roads don't always work, you can still send money with Wave. In 2017, we launched a mobile app in Senegal for cash deposit, withdrawal, and peer-to-peer and business payments. Now, we have millions of users across 9 countries and are growing fast. Our goal is to make Africa the first cashless continent and that's where you come in... How you'll help us achieve it We are growing our product design team and looking for an experienced mobile designer to expand features on our Android and iOS apps. You will have the opportunity to make financial services more accessible and inclusive for millions of people through working with thoughtful product managers, researchers, and engineers! In this role, you'll: Work closely with product managers, user researchers, engineers, and data analysts from the start to end of a feature. Create high quality designs, interactions, and prototypes to explore ideas in service of the best solution for the project (Wave uses Figma). Craft user research plans and work directly with our user researchers to identify problems and validate solutions in user testing. Contribute to Wave's design system and component library. Talk to customers and find solutions to their problems by thinking critically from their perspective. Communicate the reasoning behind your product decisions in review sessions and in conversation with PMs. Prototype visual and UX concepts and iterate towards the right solution (Wave uses Claude for mobile prototyping with Android apks). Key details This is a fully remote role. Candidates must be based in one of our hiring hubs (US, UK, Spain, Kenya, Ghana, Canada) or in one of our operating markets in Africa, including Senegal, Côte d'Ivoire, and Burkina Faso. You'll travel to one of our key markets for a 1 week immersion trip with your immediate team (Wave covers all costs). Outside of this 1 week immersion, you'll also travel to a market country with our product design lead and PMs, for a total of travel 2x a year. You're highly encouraged to visit market counties more often! We also provide a yearly stipend of $1,200 USD to meet with coworkers every year. Our salaries are competitive and are calculated using a transparent formula. For this role, we are offering a salary of up to $187,000 USD based on your location (paid in your local currency equivalent), plus a generous equity package. Major benefits: Subsidized health insurance for you and your dependents and retirement contributions (both vary from country to country) 6 months fully paid parental leave and subsidized fertility assistance Unlimited vacation with a 20-day minimum requirement, with most folks taking between 21-30 days exclusive of statutory holidays $10,000 annual charitable donation matching Requirements Experience with low and high-fidelity design & prototyping with LLMs on Android mobile apps Fluency in English. French language skills are a plus. At least 6 years of end-to-end in-house experience, with a consumer focus on product design with mobile apps. Excellent visual and interaction design skills, with an eye at removing friction from flows Attention to detail and high level of visual craft Strong illustration and animation skills. We use After Effects and Lottie at Wave but anything that can be converted to a Lottie file works Ability to deliver high-quality designs with speed and polish Bias towards action. Identify UX improvements without waiting for the perfect conditions Excellent communication and collaboration skills Ability to think through complex interaction design as well as thinking about tradeoffs of each solution Curiosity for understanding and unpacking customer behaviors and needs Experience balancing business goals, customer needs, and technical tradeoffs, while explaining your point of view to the team You might be a good fit if you Are detail-oriented and able to balance multiple projects Can iterate separate concepts quickly to user test design bets. The ability to move fast and update designs based on customer feedback is an important quality we're looking for Think carefully about in-the-weeds details and their role within the design system Feel comfortable anticipating and designing for edge cases Enjoy pairing with designers, engineers, and product managers Are excited to learn about how all our products work together Can speak, read, and write in French. This is nice to have but not a strong requirement - we have large markets in West Africa where French will come in handy. description: Menlo Security is the leader in Browser Security for human and agentic workforces. Apply strong networking fundamentals and HTTP security expertise to harden Menlo's browser isolation, proxy/gateway intercepts, and network-facing infrastructure. Partner with the MARS and AI teams to build and integrate AI agent capabilities and MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers into Menlo's security platform. Use Python or Rust to build supporting tooling, detection microservices, and prototypes alongside core C++ systems work. Deploy and operate the cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP) and orchestration (Kubernetes, Terraform) needed to run agent/MCP and threat-detection workloads reliably. Debug and optimize performance-critical, high-scale systems across the browser and supporting backend infrastructure. Collaborate cross-functionally with product, security, and AI engineering teams to ship capabilities end-to-end. Requirements: 5+ years of experience in software engineering with strong C++ systems programming skills. Strong networking fundamentals, including solid knowledge of HTTP security, web protocols and / or client-side security architecture. Relay is a technology enabled parcel carrier - we deliver parcels from retailers to end customers but do it much more efficiently than incumbents. This efficiency has propelled us into one of the fastest growing companies in Europe - we have grown over 40x in the last 18 months. The capital Relay raises decides how fast the network grows and what it can promise retailers. Raising it well, from the right investors, on terms we understand, is a job in its own right. About the role The capital we raise next decides how fast the network grows and what it can promise retailers. Our next round is planned for Q2/Q3 2027. It is for growth, from growth-stage investors, and it will be won on evidence. Today a raise runs through the CEO and the CFO alongside their day jobs. It works. It is however, not a system. You will be the person who makes it one. You will not just be the person who holds and runs the Series C transaction, but also be the Head of the Office that will build the systems to raise multiple rounds of capital in the future. Between rounds you keep the map, the materials and the investors warm, so each raise starts from a record, not a blank page. Few roles let you own how a growing company raises the capital it runs on, from the inside, round after round. Who you work with CEO: you report here. The CEO pitches and takes the decisions on a round. CFO: you work together daily. The CFO owns the budget, the forecast, internal finance and any debt. You own equity, the investors behind it, and the investor-facing model built from the CFO's numbers — never a second set. Co-founder and the Extended Leadership Team: the proof a round needs. External & Internal Counsel: terms and the close. Board: updates between rounds and approval on the round. The process start to close: the timeline, outreach, a brief before every meeting and notes after, investor questions answered within a day, and diligence. Put term sheets side by side and show what each costs in the round after. Draw up illustrative analysis and counsel the CEO on the right strategy. Hold the story in one version, drafted with the CEO. The same claims and numbers across the deck, the model and the data room. Own the investor-facing model: scenarios, unit economics and use of funds. Every number ties to one the CFO has signed. Between rounds Refresh the deck, the KPI pack and the data room every quarter. Write investor and board updates. Answer existing investors' questions. Track what we promised them. Build relationships with investors so you can source your own relationships for future rounds Read the market: who invests at our stage, on what terms, and what comparable companies showed when they raised. Put what Relay must show, and by when, to the leadership team in writing. Across both Agree in writing with each function what it produces for a raise and by when. Flag the proof the story needs a quarter early, not the week before. Keep the record: what each investor asked, what we answered, what we promised and what we learned. By the end of your first six months An investor map with a reason beside every name. One version of the story across the deck, the model and the data room. A data room refreshed every quarter, never rebuilt. A written agreement with each function on what it produces for a raise. A clear line of sight to a closed round from a ranked list of investors. What we're looking for You have run a growth-stage equity round from inside a company, or worked on several from the investing side. You want to own the process, with a view to owning the pitch and fundraising function in the future as the company scales. We don't ask for a set number of years or a particular firm on your CV. We ask for evidence. Be ready to walk us through specific rounds and your part in them. Required Round experience: you ran an equity round from inside a company, or worked on several as an investor. You can show the map you built, the order you ran it in and what you would change. Investor writing: you turn the story a founder tells in a room into a page an investor reads alone. Short, plain, in a founder's voice, with numbers that held under diligence. Modelling: you built an investor model from a company's internal forecast and defended it in diligence. Terms: you can put two term sheets side by side and say what each costs in the round after. Data rooms: you built one that answered questions before they were asked. You can name the question you missed. Getting work from other teams: you got inputs from teams that did not report to you, on dates agreed in writing. You can say what arrived late and what you did about it. Market knowledge: you know which funds invest at our stage and which partner leads, or can build that picture in weeks and show your working. Handling no: investors have told you no. You kept the record of why and used it the next time. Nice to have Experience in logistics, delivery, marketplaces or another operations-heavy business. Time at a growth-stage fund, a tech-focused bank or a private-capital adviser before going in-house. Investor relations between rounds at a private company. The hard parts The CEO pitches. You are the investors' contact for everything around the room. You are judged on how the round runs, not on the pitch. The numbers come from the CFO. The proof comes from teams that do not report to you. The market sets the timing, not us. Investors will say no, often. The record has to stay straight. The job keeps going after the close: the map, the materials in quiet quarters and the relationships between rounds. We will agree with you what support you need to do that well. How we hire Talent Acquisition, 45 minutes: the job as it is, a round you ran or worked on, and how you work. An interview with our VP International: 45 minutes: how you work, the evidence and across your whole career The case, about a day on your own time Case review, 75 minutes, with the CEO and CFO: you walk us through it, re-plan live when we change a condition, and take two questions the case cannot reach . References and a decision within a week. An offer comes in a conversation. Tell us at any stage if you need adjustments. Who Thrives at Relay?
